title.en: Yusuf and the Ripped Shirt in the House of the Aziz
title.zh: 優素福與被撕破的襯衫

region.en: Egypt, house of the Aziz (lord of the storehouses; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 埃及糧政大臣府邸（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Yusuf 12:21-34; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 12:21-34

summary.en: The buyer, an officer of Egypt, tells his wife to lodge the boy honourably — 'we may adopt him as a son.' The lady seeks him, and he resists her; God's sign turns him from evil, and when the husband finds them at the door, the wife accuses him: 'There is no punishment for a husband, unless she whose husband hath wronged her, or she is one of the erring' — but a witness suggests the proof of the shirt: if hers is torn in front she speaks truth, if behind, she lies. Torn from behind, Yusuf is cleared; she is confessed of her guilt.
summary.zh: 買者（埃及官員）命妻款待此童：『或可收為義子。』夫人勾引之，優素福拒絕。丈夫見狀，夫人誣告；見證者建議驗襯衫之證：若她前襟撕裂，她說真話；若後襟撕裂，她說謊。後襟撕裂，優素福被證清白，夫人自認其過。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And he who bought him, who was of Egypt, said to his wife, 'Give him an honourable abode; it may be that he will be useful to us, or we may adopt him as a son.' And thus did We settle the affairs of Yusuf in the land, and that We might teach him the interpreting of tales; and God is potent over his affairs, but most men know it not.

And she in whose house he was sought to seduce him, and fastened the doors, and said, 'Come hither.' He said, 'God forbid! Verily my Lord hath made my abode good. The unjust shall not prosper.' Verily she desired him, and he had desired her, had he not seen a proof of his Lord. Thus did We turn evil from him, for he was one of Our chosen servants.

And when her lord came to the door, she said, 'What shall be the punishment of one who would do evil to thy wife, but prison or a painful punishment?' Said Yusuf, 'She it was who sought to seduce me.' And a witness of her household said, 'If his shirt be torn in front, then she speaketh truth, and he is of the liars; but if it be torn behind, then she lieth, and he is of the truthful.' And when her lord saw his shirt torn behind, he said, 'This is a device of you women; truly your devices are grievous. O Yusuf, let this pass; and thou, ask pardon for thy fault, for thou hast been of the faulty.' And women of the city said, 'The wife of the Aziz hath sought her servant: he hath smitten her heart with love; we plainly see that she is in a manifest error.'

And when she heard their wiles she prepared a banquet for them, and gave to each a knife, and said to Yusuf, 'Come forth and show thyself to them.' And when they saw him they praised him greatly, and cut their hands with the knives and said, 'God keep us! This is no man: this is none other than a gracious angel.' She said, 'This is he for whom ye blamed me: I sought to seduce him, but he shrank back; and now if he doth not what I order him, he shall surely be imprisoned, and be among the abject.' He said, 'O my Lord, prison is dearer to me than that which they invite me to. And if thou turn not their wiles from me, then shall I yearn towards them and become one of the ignorant.' His Lord heard him, and turned their wiles from him: verily He is the Hearing, the Knowing.

title.en: Two Prisoners, Two Dreams: The Interpreter in the Dungeon
title.zh: 獄中二囚二夢：地牢裡的解夢者

region.zh: 埃及國家監獄（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Yusuf 12:36-42; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 12:36-42

summary.en: Two young men enter the prison with Yusuf. One dreams of pressing wine; the other dreams of birds eating bread from his head. 'Tell us its interpretation, for we see that thou art a doer of good.' Yusuf preaches first — many gods are better, or one God? — then interprets: one shall pour wine for his lord, the other shall be crucified and birds shall eat from his head. The matter is decreed; the freed man forgets Yusuf for years in the prison.
summary.zh: 二少年與優素福同入獄。一人夢榨酒，另一人夢鳥啄其頭上之餅。他們請優素福解夢；優素福先勸誡（諸神更好還是一神更好？），再釋夢：一人將為君斟酒，另一人將被釘十字架而鳥啄其頭。事已注定；獲釋者竟將優素福忘於獄中多年。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And two young men went to prison with him. One of them said, 'I saw in a dream that I was pressing wine'; and the other said, 'I saw in a dream that I was carrying bread on my head, of which the birds were eating. Tell us its interpretation, for we see that thou art a doer of good.' Yusuf answered, 'O my two fellow-prisoners, many sorts of food are better than these, and the fear of God is better... O my fellow-prisoners, are sundry lords better than the one Almighty, All-powerful God? Those whom ye worship beside Him are mere names which ye and your fathers have invented: God hath sent down no warrant for them. Judgment belongeth to God alone; He hath commanded that ye worship none but Him — the right faith; but most men know it not.'

O my two fellow-prisoners, as to one of you, he shall pour out wine for his lord to drink; and as for the other, he shall be crucified and the birds shall eat from off his head. The matter is decreed for which ye inquired. And he said to him whom he judged to be the freer of the two, 'Remember me before thy lord'; but Satan caused him to forget his Lord's remembrance, and he tarried several years in the prison.

title.en: Seven Fat Kine and Seven Green Ears: From Dungeon to Throne
title.zh: 七肥牛與七青穗：從地牢到高位

region.en: Egypt, throne hall of Pharaoh (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 埃及法老王宮（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Yusuf 12:43-57; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 12:43-57

summary.en: The king dreams that seven fat kine are devoured by seven lean, and of seven green ears of corn and seven withered. His courtiers call it 'confused dreams'; the freed prisoner remembers Yusuf at last and goes to the prison: 'Tell us of the seven fat kine...' Yusuf answers with the interpretation — seven years of plenty, then seven of hardship, then a year of release — and claims nothing for himself but that God has taught him. The king asks his freedom; the woman and the women confess, and Yusuf is set over the storehouses of Egypt.
summary.zh: 國王夢七肥牛被七瘦牛吞食，又夢七青穗與七枯穗。臣們稱之為『亂夢』；獲釋者終於想起優素福，往獄中相告。優素福釋夢：七年豐年、七年荒年、再一年解困——並自言解夢乃主所授。國王欲釋其出獄；夫人與眾婦人認罪，優素福遂掌埃及糧政。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And the king said, 'I saw in a dream seven fat kine which seven lean kine devoured; and seven green ears of corn and others withered. O chiefs, explain to me my dream, if ye can interpret a dream.' They said, 'They are confused dreams, and we do not know the interpretation of such dreams.' And he of the two who was freed, and who, after the space of years, remembered, said, 'I will tell you its interpretation, therefore send me.'

Yusuf, O man of truth, tell us of the seven fat kine which seven lean kine devoured, and of the seven green ears and the others withered, that I may return to the people, and that they may know. He said, 'Seven years shall ye sow, as ye sow: and the corn which ye reap, leave in the ear, except a little which ye eat. Then shall come after this seven grievous years, which shall eat up what ye have laid up for them, all but a little which ye shall have reserved. Then shall come after this a year of ease, in which men shall press the juice, and in which they shall return to their former state.'

And the king said, 'Bring him to me.' And when the messenger came to him he said, 'Return to thy lord and say to him, What meanest thou by the affair of the women who cut their hands? My lord knoweth their wiles.' The king said to the women, 'What was your intent when ye sought to seduce Yusuf?' They said, 'God forbid! We know no evil of him.' The wife of the Aziz said, 'Now hath the truth come to light: I seduced him, and he is of the truthful.' 'O my Lord, prison is dearer to me than that whereto these women invite me... Let me die rather; or take me out of their reach.'

And the king said, 'Bring him to me: I will take him for my own service.' And when he had conversed with him he said, 'This day shalt thou be firmly seated with us, and honoured with our trust.' And Yusuf said, 'Set me over the storehouses of the land, for I am able to keep them, and skilled to do it.' And thus did We settle Yusuf in the land, and he had possessions therein at his pleasure: We bestow Our mercy on whom We will, and We cause not the reward of the righteous to be lost.

title.en: The Cup in Benjamin's Sack and the Shirt That Restored Sight
title.zh: 便雅憫囊中金杯與復明之衣

region.en: Egyptian granary and Canaan (symbolic pin at Cairo)
region.zh: 埃及糧倉與迦南（象徵性定位於開羅）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah Yusuf 12:58-99; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 12:58-99

summary.en: Yusuf's brothers come for corn; he knows them, they know him not. He demands their brother as hostage, binds the drinking-cup in Benjamin's saddlebag, and keeps him in Egypt. Jacob weeps till his eyes whiten, yet says, 'I only complain of my grief and my sorrow to God; I know from God what ye know not.' When the brothers return, Yusuf reveals himself: 'No blame on you this day'; sends his shirt to be laid on Jacob's face — and sight returns. The family comes down to Egypt, and Yusuf raises his parents on the throne, and they fall down prostrate: the dream of the eleven stars fulfilled.
summary.zh: 優素福的兄長們來糴糧；他認得他們，他們卻不識他。他以弟弟為質，將酒杯藏於便雅憫的行囊，將他留於埃及。雅各哭到眼白，只向主訴愁。兄弟復返，優素福亮明身份：『今日你們無罪』；遣襯衫置於雅各面上——他重見光明。家眷下埃及；優素福扶父母升於寶座，眾人俯首——十一星之夢應驗。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And Yusuf's brethren came and presented themselves before him; and he knew them, but they knew him not. And when he had furnished them with their provision he said, 'Bring me a brother of yours from your father... and remember me, when ye are become settled in wealth and prosperity.' And they said, 'We will strive to obtain him from his father; verily we will do it.' And he said to his servants, 'Put their merchandise into their sacks'; and when they had done this he said to one of them, 'Place my drinking-cup in the sack of their brother Benjamin.'

And Jacob turned away from them and wept, and he said, 'O my sorrow for Yusuf!' And his eyes became white with mourning, and he was now oppressed with grief. They said, 'By God! wilt thou not cease to remember Yusuf till thou art wasted to a very skeleton, or dead?' He said, 'I only complain of my grief and my sorrow to God, and I know from God what ye know not. Go and make inquiries concerning Yusuf and his brother, and despair not of the mercy of God; for only the unbelieving despair of God's mercy.'

And when they had presented themselves they said, 'O Aziz, adversity hath visited us and our family... Restore us our brother.' And when Yusuf had clothed himself, and was going to depart, his brother said... And when they had taken their departure, Yusuf said, 'O ye men, we will demand of you your brother.' And when he had made ready their loads, he said, 'What did ye do with my drinking-cup?' They said, 'We have been unjust and guilty.' He said, 'Let no one of us be blamed this day... God forgiveth him whom He pleaseth; He is the Knowing, the Wise.'

And he said, 'This my shirt carry, and lay it on my father's face, and he shall recover his sight; then come to me with all your family.' And when the caravan had departed their father said, 'I surely smell the breath of Yusuf.' And when the bearer of the tidings came he laid it on his face and he recovered his sight, and said, 'Did I not tell you that I know from God what ye know not?' And when they came before Yusuf, he took his father to him, and said, 'Come into Egypt in safety, please God.' And he raised his parents on the throne, and they fell prostrate before him and said, 'O Yusuf, this is indeed the interpretation of my dream of aforetime: my Lord hath made it true; and He hath shown me favour, and hath brought me forth from prison, and brought you out of the desert, after that Satan had stirred up discord between me and my brethren.'

title.en: The Basket on the Nile: Musa Nursed by His Own Mother
title.zh: 尼羅河上的木箱：母親乳養的穆薩

region.en: Nile river at Pharaoh's palace, Egypt (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 埃及法老宮旁的尼羅河（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs al-Qasas 28:3-13, Ta-Ha 20:37-40; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 28:3-13

summary.en: Pharaoh exalts himself in the land and makes its people into sects, weakening a party of them, slaying their sons and sparing their women; God wills to favour the oppressed. We reveal to the mother of Musa: 'Suckle him, and when thou fearest for him, cast him into the water, and fear not nor grieve — We will restore him to thee, and make him one of Our messengers.' Pharaoh's household finds him; the wife would have him for a son. All nurses' milk is refused — then his sister says: 'Shall I show you a family who shall nurse him for you?' And so God restored him to his mother, that her eye might be refreshed and she grieve no more.
summary.zh: 法老在國中高傲，分民為派，屠男嬰而留女嬰；真主意欲恩澤受欺者。啟示穆薩之母：『哺育之；若懼，投之於水——我必還你，並立之為使者。』法老家眷拾之，其妻欲收為子。眾乳母皆不合口——其姊獻策，母子重逢，母眼復悅，不再憂傷。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: We rehearse to thee with truth a story of Moses and Pharaoh, for the sake of those who believe. Verily Pharaoh exalted himself in the earth and made its people into sects, weakening a party of them, slaying their sons and letting their women live: for he was one of the agents of corruption. And We wished to be gracious to those who were weakened in the land, and to make them leaders and to make them the heirs, and to settle a power on them in the land, and to show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts what they feared from them.

And We revealed to the mother of Moses: 'Suckle him, and when thou fearest for him, cast him into the water, and fear not and grieve not, for We will restore him to thee, and we will make him one of Our messengers.' And the family of Pharaoh found him, and he became to them an enemy and a sorrow; for Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts were sinners. And Pharaoh's wife said, 'This boy shall be a delight to my eye and to thee — slay him not; haply he may be useful to us, or we may take him for a son; and they knew not what they did.'

And in the morning an iniquitous affliction came on the heart of the mother of Moses: verily she had all but made him public, had We not confirmed her heart that she might be one of the believers. And she said to his sister, 'Follow him.' And she watched him from afar off, and they perceived it not. And they prevented his being nursed by the nurses, until his sister came and said, 'Shall I point out to you a family who shall nurse him for you and who shall advise him?' And thus We restored him to his mother, that her eye might be refreshed, and that she might not be grieved, and that she might know that the promise of God is true.

title.en: The Slaying of the Egyptian and Flight to Midian

region.en: Egyptian town and Midian wells (symbolic pin at Sinai oasis)
region.zh: 埃及城鎮與米甸水井（象徵性定位於西奈綠洲）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Qasas 28:14-28; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 28:14-28

summary.en: Musa comes to manhood, endowed with wisdom and knowledge. Going into the city unmarked, he finds two fighting, one of his party and one of his foes, and the oppressed calls on him for help; he strikes the Egyptian and kills him. 'This is the work of Satan; he is a manifest misleader.' A man from the far end of the city brings word that the chiefs are plotting to slay him; he flies to Midian. At the well, two girls drive back their flock; he waters for them, and their father offers him eight or ten years of service for a marriage portion — and he takes the road to Egypt again, 'with a watchful eye.'
summary.zh: 穆薩成年，智慧知識俱足。入城遇兩人相鬥，受欺者求援；他擊倒埃及人。『此乃魔之所為——他確是明顯的迷誤者。』城中遠端有人報信：長老們欲殺他。他逃往米甸。井旁見二女驅羊後退，他為她們飲羊；其父以八年或十年為聘，許女嫁之。他重返埃及之路，『眼觀四方』。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And when Moses came to full age and strength, We endowed him with wisdom and knowledge: and thus do We reward the beneficent. And he entered the city at a time when its inhabitants were careless of him, and there he found two men fighting, the one of his own religion and the other of his foes; and he who was of his own religion called on him for help against him who was of his foes. And Moses struck him with his fist and killed him. He said, 'This is the work of Satan; and he is a manifest and open misleader.'

He said, 'O my Lord, I have unjustly slain a soul, therefore forgive me.' And God forgave him; for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. He said, 'O my Lord, because thou hast forgiven me and shown me favour, I will never again be the helper of the guilty.' And in the morning he was in the city, fearing and cautious; and he who had asked his help the day before, cried out to him for help. Moses said to him, 'Truly thou art a manifest deceiver.'

And when he would have laid hands on him who was an enemy to them both, he said, 'O Moses, dost thou desire to slay me, as thou didst slay a person yesterday? Thou desirest nothing but to become a tyrant in this land, and desirest not to become a director of the right.' And a man came from the city's remotest part, running, and said, 'O Moses, the chiefs are deliberating about thee, to slay thee; depart hence; I am one of those who wish thee well.' And he went out of the city, afraid and cautious, and said, 'O Lord, deliver me from the unjust people.'

And when he came to the waters of Midian he found a company of men watering, and he found beside them two women keeping back their flocks. He said, 'What are ye about?' They said, 'We cannot water our flocks until the shepherds drive off theirs; and our father is very old.' And he watered their flocks, then turned back into the shade, and said, 'O my Lord, I stand in need of the good which thou shalt send down to me.' And the daughters came to him... and their father said, 'I desire to marry thee to one of these my two daughters on condition that thou serve me eight years, or if thou complete ten, it shall be of thy own free gift.' He said, 'Let it be so between me and thee: whichever of the two terms I fulfil, let there be no injustice to me; and God is witness of what I say.' And Moses said, 'Now will I depart with a watchful eye.'

title.en: The Burning Bush in Tuwa: 'Verily I Am Thy Lord'
title.zh: 圖窪的焚荊棘：「我確是你的主」

region.en: Tuwa, the sacred valley of Mount Sinai (literal pin)
region.zh: 西奈山聖谷圖窪（實際定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs Ta-Ha 20:9-24, al-Qasas 28:29-35, al-Qasas 27:7-12; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 20:9-24 and 28:29-35

summary.en: After the term is fulfilled, Moses journeys with his family and sees a fire in the valley of Tuwa. 'I see a fire: haply I may bring you a lighted brand, or may find guidance at the fire.' The voice calls: 'Moses! I am thy Lord — put off thy shoes, for thou art in the sacred valley Tuwa.' He is given two signs: the rod that becomes a serpent, and the hand white but unharmed, thrust into the bosom. 'Go to Pharaoh, for he hath rebelled.' 'And my brother Aaron — make him my helper.' 'Thou shalt be aided through thy brother.'
summary.zh: 穆薩攜家旅行，見圖窪谷中有火光：『或可取火，或可尋得指引。』有聲呼喚：『穆薩！我確是你的主——脫掉你的鞋，你確在聖谷圖窪。』賜兩件徵兆：杖化蛇，手入懷則白而無害。『去見法老，他確已暴虐。』『求你使兄長亞倫相助。』『你必得兄之助。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the divine speech at the burning bush; public-domain translation.

passages.text: Hath the story of Moses reached thee? When he saw a fire, and said to his family, 'Wait ye here, for I see a fire in the distance; haply I may bring you a lighted brand from it, or may find at the fire some guidance.' And when he came up to it, a voice called to him, 'O Moses, verily I am thy Lord; therefore put off thy shoes, for thou art in the sacred valley Tuwa. And I have chosen thee: hearken then to what shall be revealed.

Verily I am God: there is no God but Me: therefore worship Me, and observe prayer in my remembrance... And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses? He said, 'It is my staff: I lean on it; and with it I beat down leaves for my flock; and other uses have I for it.' He said, 'Cast it down, O Moses.' And he cast it down, and behold it became a serpent which ran along. He said, 'Take it and fear not: We will restore it to its former state. And put thy hand into thy bosom: it shall come forth white, but unharmed: — another sign... Go thou to Pharaoh, for he hath rebelled with excess of rebellion.'

And when he came up to it he was called: 'O Moses, verily I am thy Lord; therefore put off thy shoes, for thou art in the sacred valley Tuwa... And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses? He said, 'It is my staff: on it I lean; and with it I beat down leaves for my flock.' He said, 'Cast it down, O Moses.' And he cast it down, and behold, it was a serpent that ran along. He said, 'Take it and fear not: We will restore it to its former state.' He said, 'My Lord, I have slain a man of them, and I fear lest they slay me; and my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I; send him therefore with me as an aider to confirm me; verily I fear that they will treat me as an impostor.' God said, 'We will strengthen thine arm by thy brother, and they shall not touch you: with Our signs, ye twain and those who follow you, shall be victorious.'

title.en: The Magicians Cast Down: Serpents, Belief, and the Gibbet
title.zh: 眾術士俯首：蛇變、歸信與十字架

region.zh: 埃及法老前的競技場（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs ash-Shu'ara 26:10-51, al-A'raf 7:103-126; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 26:10-51

summary.en: Pharaoh assembles the magicians for a day of festival; they ask, 'Shall we have a reward if we conquer?' Moses says, 'Cast what ye have to cast'; and they cast down their cords and staves — and through their magic it seemed to him that they were running. Then Moses casts his rod, and it swallows up their lying shows. The magicians fall prostrate: 'We believe in the Lord of all creatures, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.' Pharaoh threatens the gibbet and mutilation; they answer that their Lord's grace they have already attained, 'and Thou art the vengeful of the vengeful.'
summary.zh: 法老召集術士於節日；他們問：『若得勝可有賞？』穆薩說：『扔下你們要扔的。』繩杖落地——幻術之中似在奔跑。穆薩擲杖，杖竟吞其所現。術士俯首：『我們信萬物之主、穆薩與亞倫之主。』法老以磔刑斷手相威；他們答：『我主之恩已獲；你是報復者中之報復者。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And when Moses said, 'Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of all creatures; I speak to you only what is true: send away with me the children of Israel.' He said, 'Did we not nurture thee among us as a child? And thou didst dwell among us years of thy life... and thou hast done the deed which thou hast done, and thou hast been of the ungrateful.' He said, 'I did it indeed, and I was one of those who erred... and I fled from you when I feared you, but my Lord hath given me judgment, and hath made me one of His Apostles.'

Pharaoh said, 'If thou puttest forth any god, other than me, I will certainly make thee one of the imprisoned.' Moses said, 'What! though I show thee that which is manifest?' He said, 'Show it me then, if thou art of the truthful.' So he threw down his rod, and lo, it was a serpent which moved along; and he drew out his hand, and lo, it was white to the beholders. Pharaoh said to his nobles, 'Truly this is a skilled enchanter: he wisheth to drive you out of your land by his enchantments; what do ye advise?' They said, 'Put him and his brother off for a while, and send to the cities men who shall assemble all the skilful magicians.'

And the magicians came to Pharaoh: 'Shall we indeed be rewarded if we conquer?' He said, 'Yes, and moreover shall ye be of those near my person.' They said, 'O Moses, wilt thou first throw down thy rod, or shall we throw down ours?' Moses said, 'Do ye throw it down first'; and when they threw it down they enchanted the eyes of the people, and dismayed them, for they had wrought a great feat of magic. Then We revealed to Moses, 'Throw down thy rod'; and lo, it swallowed up what they had devised of falsehood. So the enchanters fell down prostrate and said, 'We believe in the Lord of all creatures, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.'

Pharaoh said, 'Ye believe on Him before I have given you leave! Verily this is a device which ye have devised in this city, that ye may drive out its inhabitants... But I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you all.' They said, 'Verily we shall return to our Lord; but Thou takest vengeance on us only because we have believed on the signs of our Lord when they have come to us. O our Lord, pour out upon us patience, and make us die in submission to thy will.'

title.en: The Sea Divide: Pharaoh Drowns Watching the Signs
title.zh: 海水分開：法老溺亡於追擊

region.en: Red Sea crossing, Gulf of Suez (literal pin)
region.zh: 紅海渡越，蘇伊士灣（實際定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surahs ash-Shu'ara 26:52-68, Ta-Ha 20:77-79; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 26:52-68

summary.en: We reveal to Moses: 'Go forth with my servants by night, for ye will be pursued.' Pharaoh sends heralds into the cities: 'These are a small company, yet they have enraged us, and we are a numerous host, watchful.' The two parties come in sight of one another, and the followers of Moses say, 'We shall certainly be pursued.' 'By no means, for my Lord is with me: He will guide me.' The sea is cleft in two — each way like a great rampart — and the others are made to follow: the whole host is drowned. Pharaoh says, 'I believe that there is no God but He in whom the children of Israel believe... and I am of those who submit' — 'What! now? when hitherto thou hast rebelled and been of the doers of damage.' The body is left on the shore a sign to after times.
summary.zh: 啟示穆薩：『夜間率僕出走，你們必被追趕。』法老遣使於諸城：『此輩人少，卻激怒我們；我們人多勢眾。』兩軍相望，隨從者言：『我們必被追上。』『不然，我的主同我在一起，他將引導。』海分為二——各如巨大城垣——法老追隨而入，全軍覆沒。臨溺之際，法老信而順服——『現在才信嗎？你早已悖逆。』其屍留於岸，以為後世之鑒。

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the drowning of Pharaoh is treated within Islam as a historical deliverance; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And We revealed to Moses, saying, 'Go forth with my servants by night, for ye will be pursued.' And Pharaoh sent heralds into the cities: 'Verily these are a small company, and they have enraged us; and we are a numerous host well prepared.' So We compelled them to quit their gardens and their fountains, and their treasures and their splendid dwellings. Thus it was: and We gave them to the children of Israel for an inheritance.

And the people of Pharaoh pursued them at sunrise. And when the two parties were within sight of one another, those who were with Moses said, 'We shall surely be pursued.' Moses said, 'By no means, for my Lord is with me, and will guide me.' And We revealed to Moses, saying, 'Smite the sea with thy rod.' And when he smote it, it was divided into two parts, and each part was like a huge mound. And We made the others to come up in that place; and We saved Moses and all who were with him; and We drowned the others.

Pharaoh said, 'O chiefs, I know not that ye have any god beside me: light a fire for me, O Haman, and bake clay, and build me a tower that I may mount up to the God of Moses; for verily I think that he is a liar.' And the drowning overtook him: 'I believe that there is no God but He in whom the children of Israel believe, and I am of those who submit to Him.' 'What! now? when hitherto thou hast rebelled and been of the doers of damage. This day will We save thee in thy body only, that thou mayest be a sign to those who shall come after thee: for verily many among mankind are regardless of Our signs.'

title.en: Musa and Khidr at the Meeting of the Two Seas
title.zh: 穆薩與花德爾於兩海交會處

region.en: Al-Majma', the place where the two seas meet (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 兩海交會之處（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Qur'an revealed c. 610-632 CE; Surah al-Kahf 18:60-82; Rodwell 1861

source.work: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), trans. J. M. Rodwell, 1861, Sura 18:60-82

summary.en: Moses says to his servant, 'I will not cease until I reach the place where the two seas meet, though I journey years.' At the rock they forget the fish, which takes its way in the sea; at morning Moses says, 'This is the very place.' They find one of Our servants whom God has taught knowledge from Himself. Moses asks to follow and learn; the man warns, 'Thou canst not bear with me patiently — how canst thou bear what thou hast not comprehended?' Three deeds follow: the scuttled ship, the slain boy, the raised wall. And the meaning: the ship belonged to poor toilers, a tyrant king was at sea; the boy was bound for evil deeds and unbelief; the wall was orphans', their treasure beneath — 'thy Lord willed that they should reach their maturity and bring forth their treasure as a mercy from thy Lord. And I did it not of mine own accord.'
summary.zh: 穆薩對僕人說：『我必行至兩海交會處，縱行多年。』至磐石處忘了魚，魚遂入海；清晨穆薩道：『此即其所。』遇主之僕，主曾以己之知識授之。穆薩求隨從學習；對方警告：『你不能耐我——你何能耐所不解之事？』三事隨之：鑿船、殺童、扶牆。義理：船乃貧者之財，海上暴君將奪；童子父母皆信主，恐其悖逆忘恩；牆屬孤兒，寶藏於下——『你的主意欲他們成年取出寶藏，出於你的主的恩慈。並非我自作主張。』

sensitivity.note: Sacred text of a living tradition; the identity of the 'servant of God' (Khidr) is a matter of tafsir tradition; public-domain translation.

passages.text: And when Moses said to his servant, 'I will not cease until I reach the place where the two seas meet, though I journey years'; and when they had reached the meeting-place of the two seas, they forgot their fish, and he took his way in the sea freely. And when they had passed on, Moses said to his servant, 'Bring us our morning meal, for we are weary with this journey.' He said, 'Dost thou see what has happened? When we repaired to the rock for repose, then verily I forgot the fish — and none but Satan caused me to forget it — and he took his way into the sea in a wondrous sort.' Moses said, 'It was for this we waited'; and they went back again, retracing their footsteps.

Then they found one of Our servants unto whom We had given mercy from Ourself, and unto whom We had given knowledge proceeding from Ourself. And Moses said to him, 'Shall I follow thee, that thou mayest teach me, for instruction's sake, some of what thou hast been taught?' He said, 'Verily thou wilt be unable to bear with me patiently: and how canst thou bear patiently that which thou hast not comprehended?' Moses said, 'If I ask thee aught concerning this, when thou hast taught me, then befriend me not: thou hast an excuse for leaving me.'

They proceeded on their way until they embarked on board a vessel, and he scuttled it. 'What! hast thou scuttled it that thou mayest drown its crew? Now hast thou done a strange thing.' He said, 'Did I not tell thee that thou couldst not bear with me patiently?' And they travelled on till they met a youth, and he slew him. Moses said, 'Hast thou slain him who is innocent, and for no cause? Now hast thou wrought a grievous thing.' And they travelled on till they came to a city, and they asked its food of the inhabitants, but they refused them hospitality... And they found there a wall which was about to fall, and he set it upright.

He said, 'This is the parting between me and thee. I will tell thee the meaning of that which thou couldst not bear with patience. As to the vessel, it belonged to poor men who toiled upon the sea; and I was minded to render it unsound, for there was after them a king who seized every vessel by force. And as to the youth, his parents were believers, and we feared lest he should stir them up to rebellion and unbelief; and we desired that their Lord might give them in his place a child more pure than he, and more kindly. And as to the wall, it belonged to two orphan youths of the city, and beneath it was a treasure hidden which belonged to them; and their father was a righteous man: and thy Lord willed that they should reach the age of strength and bring forth their treasure as a mercy from thy Lord. And I did it not of mine own accord: such is the interpretation of that which thou couldst not bear with patience.'
